root_idea.summary: The root centers on drawing something out with force, shaking it loose, and removing it from its base.
root_idea.development: The physical image of pulling and loosening extends to the Quranic raising of the mountain, the slackening or displacement of a load's fastenings, a woman from whom many children are drawn, and a flint that produces fire by analogy.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To pull something up and dislodge it from its base; to raise it forcefully.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the object is the mountain, which is raised above the people; the usage conveys forceful removal or lifting rather than ordinary elevation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tug at or displace something so that its fastenings become slack; said of the ties or loops of a load when the load is shaken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional physical construction describing the loosening of a load's securing ties through pulling or displacement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prolific in childbearing; said of a woman who has many children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension in which children are conceived as being drawn or brought forth from the woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Producing fire; said of a flint that gives a spark or catches fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative comparison with the prolific woman, based on the production or bringing forth of something.
